title: From All That Dwell Below the Skies
description: From All That Dwell Below the Skies in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 63, “Doxology”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From all that dwell be-low the skies Let the Cre-a-tor's praise a-rise! Let the Re-deem-er's name be sung, Through ev-ery land, by ev-ery tongue!

lines: From all that dwell below the skies
Let the Redeemer's name be sung,
Through every land, by every tongue!
Thy praise shall sound from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
